audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL-centric logic (EVM opcodes, gas economics, transaction lifecycle, contract creation, state transitions across multiple forks) and the EL-CL interface (deposit request extraction, Engine API). CL is in scope where it interfaces with EL.

out_of_scope: Beacon Chain state transitions (except deposit processing)

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal component: the Ethereum client calling the EVMC module is the system under audit itself, not an external entity.
Internal component: the EVM opcode dispatcher is an internal execution engine component, not an external data source.
Internal component: represents the currently executing smart contract context within the EVM, not an external entity.
Internal component: a smart contract implementing replay protection is executing within the EVM, not sending data from outside.
Internal component: a contract invoking a precompile is internal EVM execution, not an external data source.
Governance actor: client implementation teams are not runtime data sources that send data into the system at execution time.
Governance actor: node operators are not runtime data sources; they configure nodes but do not send data into the protocol at execution time.
Governance actor: core developers make protocol decisions but do not send runtime data into the system.
Governance actor: EIP authors propose specifications but do not send runtime data into the system.
External verifier: on-chain contracts verifying merkle proofs consume data from the system but do not send data INTO the system boundary for processing.
External verifier: hardware wallets verify proofs externally but do not send data into the consensus/execution system boundary.
External verifier: off-chain verifiers consume proofs but do not inject data into the system under audit.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit transactions via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. All transaction data is potentially malicious: malformed RLP, invalid signatures, resource exhaustion attempts, oversized init code, etc. Consolidates EXT-USER, EXT-TX-SUBMITTER, EXT-TX-SENDER, EXT-SIGNER from source subgraphs.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer Node via devp2p
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P Network (devp2p: blocks, transactions, SSZ-encoded data)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes propagate blocks, transactions, and serialized data over unauthenticated P2P channels. Any peer could be malicious: sending invalid blocks, malformed transactions, oversized SSZ data (DoS via ProgressiveList), or eclipse attack attempts. Consolidates EXT-PEER, EXT-NETWORK-PEER, EXT-P2P-GOSSIP from source subgraphs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer (Miner/Validator)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block submission via P2P or Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers submit blocks containing transactions, state roots, and receipts. Blocks must be fully validated: header checks, ommer validation, transaction execution, root hash verification. A malicious producer could include invalid transactions, manipulate gas limits, or forge state roots. Consolidates EXT-MINER from source subgraphs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The CL communicates with EL over JWT-authenticated Engine API. The channel is authenticated, but payload content (execution payloads, fork choice state) must still be validated. The CL could provide payloads with invalid state transitions. Consolidates EXT-CONSENSUS-LAYER from source subgraphs.

trusted_external_entities.name: Deposit Contract via Event Logs
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Transaction receipt logs from deposit contract (0x00000000219ab540356cbb839cbe05303d7705fa)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The deposit contract is a trusted on-chain contract, but its log data crosses a trust boundary when extracted for CL processing. The EL must validate deposit event data format (576 bytes, correct offsets/sizes) before forwarding to CL. The contract itself is immutable and audited, but log parsing must be robust against edge cases.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via P2P (Archetypal CL Threat)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal CL attack vector. Malicious validators may propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations (slashing conditions), or attempt censorship. All CL P2P data requires full validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: External MEV/Relay Service (Archetypal CL Threat)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: External APIs (MEV-Boost relay, checkpoint sync endpoints)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal CL attack vector. External services like MEV-Boost relays or checkpoint sync endpoints could provide incorrect data, censor transactions, or cause denial of service. Data from these services must never be trusted without verification.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required: RLP decoding, signature verification (including EIP-2718 type byte in signed data for typed transactions), nonce check, balance sufficiency, gas limit check, init code size limits (CREATE/CREATE2). Must reject malformed typed transactions with invalid type bytes (EIP-2718).

Access list entries must be validated and gas charged correctly. Malicious access lists could attempt to warm arbitrary storage slots. Gas accounting for access list entries must be correct to prevent underpricing attacks.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Block validation pipeline (header, ommer, body, root verification)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full block validation required: header field validation, ommer validity (max 2, age 1-6), transaction execution, state/transaction/receipt root hash verification. Must reject blocks with invalid PoW (pre-merge) or invalid state transitions.
Same validation as JSON-RPC submitted transactions. Additionally must handle P2P-specific DoS vectors: flooding with invalid transactions, oversized payloads.
Length validation must occur BEFORE full decoding to prevent DoS via oversized ProgressiveList data. Runtime limits must be enforced even though ProgressiveList is unbounded in schema.
Block producer output must be fully validated. Gas limit must be within parent +/- parent/1024 and >= minimum. All transactions must be valid. State roots must match computed values.

JWT authentication verified. Execution payload content must still be validated: block structure, transaction validity, state transition correctness. Fork choice updates must reference valid block hashes.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Deposit request extraction from transaction receipts (EIP-7685)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Deposit event data must be exactly 576 bytes with correct ABI offsets (pubkey@160/48B, withdrawal_creds@256/32B, amount@320/8B, signature@384/96B, index@512/8B). InvalidBlock on any mismatch. Only logs from the canonical deposit contract address with correct event signature topic are processed.

All proposed blocks and attestations must be validated against consensus rules. Conflicting attestations must trigger slashing conditions. Censorship resistance depends on sufficient honest validator participation.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: MEV-Boost relay API / checkpoint sync endpoint
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Data from external relays and sync endpoints must be verified against on-chain state. Checkpoint sync data must be validated against known finalized state. MEV relay payloads must pass full block validation.
